input.quote: 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
input.rationale: § 2.1 imposes a three-year, USD 2,000,000-per-year take-or-pay commitment expressly "without reduction or termination rights" — squarely the walk-away position (multi-year take-or-pay with no reduction or termination right) and well short of the fallback (single 12-month commitment, reducible on 30 days' notice, true-up rather than penalty). It also contradicts § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges that Customer "has made no ... minimum-volume ... commitment," and sits awkwardly with our § 9.4 convenience-termination right and § 7.1's bar on minimum-use charges. We therefore replaced § 2.1 with the preferred position: no minimum purchase or volume commitment and payment only for Services used or ordered, which also resolves the internal conflict with § 12.3. Retained § 9.4 language about a "committed term" only restricts Vendor and remains harmless.

mappings.element: Customer has no minimum purchase or volume commitment.
Customer pays only for usage or ordered Services.

proposal.summary: Remove the three-year USD 2M take-or-pay commitment and confirm Customer pays only for usage or ordered Services.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We removed the multi-year take-or-pay commitment in § 2.1, which our playbook treats as walk-away territory and which contradicts § 12.3's acknowledgement that we made no minimum-volume commitment; § 2.1 now confirms we pay only for Services used or ordered. If a commitment is essential, our fallback is a single 12-month commitment reducible on 30 days' notice with a true-up rather than a shortfall penalty.
